title: Operating machinery in permanently shadowed regions at -230 C
bottleneck: The Moon's most valuable water ice sits in permanently shadowed craters at -230 C, where regolith is concrete-hard, lubricants freeze solid, metals turn brittle, and solar power is unavailable by definition. Equipment must survive thermal extremes, operate in darkness, and communicate without line-of-sight to Earth. Every mechanism — drills, excavators, seals, electronics — needs cryogenic-rated redesign, and failures cannot be serviced.
why_it_blocks: PSRs are the richest known lunar resource deposits; if machines cannot work there, the lunar water economy is limited to trace hydrated minerals elsewhere — a far poorer resource base.
current_state: The VIPER rover, designed for PSR prospecting, was cancelled in 2024; commercial landers target sunlit areas. No mission has operated inside a permanently shadowed region.
